subject: Proposal: tiered cash remedies for recurring partial degradation
messages:
From: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-10T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. CareBridge leadership is comfortable with the basic uptime credits language, but Legal & Procurement pushed back asking for stronger economic remedies if a degradation pattern emerges. Their ask is not for an unlimited liability clause, but a small, structured cash-at-risk ladder that kicks in for repeated regional/partial degradations that materially affect throughput (e.g., repeated 5–15 minute regional latency spikes during business hours).

Specifically, they proposed:
- After 3 separate incidents in a 90-day window (severity: partial degradation, not full outage), 5% of the monthly committed fee held at risk for 30 days.
- After 5 incidents in 90 days, a 15% holdback and a right to terminate for convenience with a 60-day cure/cash buyout.

They say credits are fine for single incidents, but patterns warrant stronger deterrents. They also asked for access to SLO logs and one month of request traces to validate incidents.

Can your team share whether Redwood would consider a limited, tiered cash-hold and a corresponding termination right? If not, is there an operational alternative (enhanced monitoring + automatic routing to Dedicated capacity + longer notice windows) we can propose?

I've attached the procurement team's proposed SLA excerpt for context.

Best,
Megan
Procurement Lead, CareBridge Health

Attachment: CB-SLA-Excerpt-v2.docx
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear write-up and the excerpt. Good questions.

Short answer: we try to avoid cash penalties beyond credits because they create open-ended financial exposure and make underwriting (and Dedicated capacity commitments) hard, but we do offer structured mitigations that can address their intent.

Options we can propose now:
1) Pattern-based escalations: automatic Dedicated routing for a customer after N incidents in a rolling window, plus an SLA uplift (reduces likelihood of recurrence).
2) Escrowed fee-at-risk (capped): hold a pre-agreed capped amount in escrow under very specific triggers; the amount is limited and there is a firm cure timetable.
3) Operational evidence package: provide SLO logs, trace excerpts, and a post-incident RCA; we can include an audit window but with defined redaction for customer data.

If they insist on a cash ladder, we can potentially accept a narrowly-scoped escrow cap and a one-time right to terminate if cures fail — provided the triggers are operationally verifiable and the cap is modest (e.g., 15% monthly cap overall). I will loop in Marissa from Legal to weigh in on contract language and ben for pricing impact.

Quick Q: Do they want the termination right to apply only to the service level (ability to stop routing requests) or to the whole contract? That changes negotiation posture.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>, logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Megan — thanks for sharing the procurement language.

From Legal's perspective, we're open to a narrowly-drawn escrow/capped cash-hold approach if we can get the following safeguards:
- Clear, objective incident definitions (latency thresholds, regional scope, business hours definition).
- Exclusion for incidents caused by: customer misconfiguration, third-party cloud provider maintenance, DDoS beyond our mitigation SLA, or force majeure.
- A definite cap (aggregate cap per 12-month period) and a maximum single-event cap.
- Cure periods with operational remedies (Dedicated routing, capacity uplift) before termination right vests.
- A requirement that claims be supported by the SLO evidence package we generate; Redwood reserves the right to redact PII.

We would not accept open-ended liquidated damages. If CareBridge wants termination, it must be carefully conditioned — e.g., a termination right only after escrow exhaustion and failed cure attempts.

I note the proposed percentages in your excerpt; 5% then 15% could be workable if tied to clear triggers and capped. I'll draft suggested language and share a tracked-change excerpt.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Dir., Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: Aaron Kim <aaron.kim@carebridge-health.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Marissa, Logan — thanks. Helpful framing. A few clarifications from our side:
- The termination right would be a customer right to terminate the overall contract for convenience (not just traffic routing) after the prescribed cures fail and escrow is exhausted. They recognize this is a heavy ask — they want it as a remote deterrent.
- They want the incident counting to ignore major cloud provider outages and to include a 14-day cure window after each incident.
- They also asked for one month of request traces and 12 months of SLO history during diligence to baseline the current behavior.

We attached the original procurement slide they sent. Happy to have Ben join a call next week to discuss trade-offs.

Best,
Megan

Attachment: SLO-logs-apr.zip
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>, logan.wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-20T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Appreciate the detail — quick pricing/ops take:
- Escrow/capped hold: we can model a capped escrow equal to 25% of one month minimum commitment, released progressively unless triggers are met. This keeps our balance sheet exposure bounded.
- Cure pathway: during the 14-day cure, we offer (A) priority routing to Dedicated capacity for the customer, (B) an incident RCA and mitigation plan within 72 hours, and (C) a one-time credits top-up for the period of degraded performance.
- Termination: if escrow exhausted and cures fail, termination for convenience with a 60-day notice and a cash buyout equal to the remaining 2 months of committed spend (capped at the escrow aggregate).

I'll put numbers on paper and propose two alternatives for the call: (1) operational-first (Dedicated + monitoring + credits), (2) hybrid (small capped escrow + operational triggers + limited termination right).

Shall we schedule a 30-minute negotiation call with CareBridge legal on April 26?

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Megan Tolley <megan.tolley@carebridge-health.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — cash remedies for partial degradation

Thanks all — April 26 works, can we make it April 27 instead? Our counsel has a conflict on the 26.

We reviewed Ben's outline internally. CareBridge prefers the hybrid option but wants the escrow cap at 30% of one month minimum committed spend and the termination buyout to be no more than a single month of committed spend (their CFO wants a lower buyout). They also asked that Redwood provide a sanitized SLO pack (redacted traces) for the prior 12 months and confirm whether Dedicated routing can be applied automatically after the third incident (without separate order).

Looking forward to the call — please send an updated term-sheet ahead of the meeting.

Best,
Megan
CareBridge Health
